content.text: {"heavy-calm":"Look at the single faded bloom near the top right, gone grey among all that blue. Van Gogh let it stay, and if you are feeling low and quiet, it is a small, honest sign that sorrow has a place even in a bright bouquet.","mid-calm":"The pale wall behind the flowers is laid down in short, patient strokes, like breath settling. It gives the eye somewhere unhurried to rest between the blooms, which suits an even, easy mood.","bright-calm":"A plain white jug on a cool green table holds everything steady here. The softness of that pale background and the gentle blues of the petals make a warm, restful company for a light heart.","heavy-mid":"This is not a grave painting, but it is a thoughtful one: the irises crowd and lean as if their weight is almost too much for the jug. If you are carrying something heavy, the picture meets you there and then lifts it toward color.","mid-mid":"There is a steady balance in how the green blade-like leaves fan out on both sides of the jug. It is an everyday still life, a vase on a table, painted with enough care to make an ordinary day feel well kept.","bright-mid":"The blues here are deep but never cold, and the flowers spill over the right edge of the jug as if they could not wait. That easy abundance sits naturally with a hopeful, warm mood.","heavy-charged":"You will not find a storm in this picture, and that is the point of it for you. The sharp, upward leaves carry real tension, yet they are held by a calm white jug and a quiet wall, a counterweight when things feel too loud.","mid-charged":"Every petal is pushed on with thick, restless paint, and the stems shoot out in all directions. If your energy is running high, the irises share that alertness while giving it a shape you can rest your eyes on.","bright-charged":"Watch the one iris at the top left lifting clear of the bunch, as if it is reaching for more air. The whole bouquet has that lift, a quiet joy rather than a loud one, and it keeps pace with an exuberant mood."}

{"heavy-calm":"This panther will not sit still with you, but its solid black body against the pale cream ground has a gravity you might recognize. Think of it as a counterweight: something coiled and alive to keep near a quiet, inward stretch.","mid-calm":"The cream background is wide and open, and that empty space gives the crouching cat room to breathe. It is a lively poster, though, so it meets an unhurried mood as a small spark rather than a mirror.","bright-calm":"Honestly, this is more alert than restful, with green eyes fixed straight on you. What it offers a gentle mood is warmth in the red lettering and a hint of play in that long curling tail.","heavy-mid":"Look at the open red mouth and the white teeth: there is real tension here, the weight of an animal about to move. It suits a grave, thoughtful frame of mind by holding that moment just before something happens.","mid-mid":"Bold red letters, one black animal, a plain cream field. The design is clear and direct in an everyday way, with enough bite in the panther's stare to keep it from ever feeling ordinary.","bright-mid":"The red BROOKFIELD arching over the cat's back reads like a friendly invitation to a day out. If you are feeling hopeful and easy, that cheerful lettering balances the snarl beneath it.","heavy-charged":"Those green eyes and bared fangs carry the stormy edge you are feeling, and the cat's low, spread crouch looks ready to spring. It is drama held in flat shapes, defiant and compact.","mid-charged":"Every line here is restless, from the thin white outlines tracing the muscles to the clawed paw reaching past the letters. It matches an alert, energized mood by looking like it is already in motion.","bright-charged":"There is something playful in how the panther sprawls across the poster, tail flicking up toward the corner and paws spilling out of frame. The punchy red ZOO lettering adds the lively, exuberant note."}

{"heavy-calm":"This poster is louder than your mood, built around an orange lightning bolt cracking down from the top corner. What may suit you is the small child at the bottom, seated and absorbed in a toy, a quiet figure who stays still while the danger is turned away above him.","mid-calm":"For an unhurried frame of mind, look past the jagged bolt to the soft, mottled blue printed behind the child, like clouds rubbed onto paper. The drama is real, but the boy sits calmly in it, and that small calm is what this work can offer you.","bright-calm":"This one is not gentle at heart, and it would be wrong to pretend otherwise. If you want warmth, it lives in the cream paper and the boy's round, rosy face as he plays, kept safe while the storm overhead is blocked.","heavy-mid":"The words DIPHTHERIA STRIKES UNPROTECTED CHILDREN sit stacked at the top in orange, blue and brown, grave and plain. It shares your weightiness, a public warning from the Chicago Department of Health that treats a real threat with seriousness instead of panic.","mid-mid":"There is a steady, practical logic here: danger above, a blue disc marked TOXOID catching it, a child below. If you feel balanced and everyday, you may like how clearly the poster sorts trouble from protection in three simple layers.","bright-mid":"Hope is the point of this poster, even if it arrives through alarm. The blue shield takes the orange bolt head on with a burst of sparks, and the boy below never has to look up, which is a reassuring picture for an easy, hopeful day.","heavy-charged":"You will find your tension in the orange zigzag, sharp as a strike of lightning, slamming into the tilted blue disc. It is a stormy image with a defiant core, showing the hit and the block in the same instant.","mid-charged":"Restless energy runs all through this design, from the speed lines trailing behind the spinning disc to the bold block letters stacked like a shout. It matches an alert mood with a feeling that something is happening right now and someone is ready for it.","bright-charged":"This poster is more tense than joyful, so its lift comes from defiance rather than delight. The bright orange TOXOID across the bottom and the shield flinging off the bolt give your lively mood something to cheer: a fight that is being won."}

{"heavy-calm":"This poster will not match your stillness; its red-orange field and stacked shapes are loud from edge to edge. If you want something to sit beside a quiet, heavy day and nudge it gently outward, the small cream circle drifting near the top lettering is a calm place to rest your eye first.","mid-calm":"Honestly, this is a busier picture than your mood, crowded with rovers, domes and zigzags. What it offers an unhurried mind is order: every shape is flat and cleanly placed, so the energy reads as tidy rather than frantic.","bright-calm":"The warmth you carry is here in the color, a sun-baked red under soft yellows and cream. The pace is quicker than yours, but the wheat stalks rising at the lower right have a gentle, growing feel that fits a light heart.","heavy-mid":"If your thoughts are weighty, this poster works as a counterweight rather than a mirror. The cheerful promise of \"Historic Sites\" on a planet no one has walked turns a grave question about our future into something curious and almost funny.","mid-mid":"For an ordinary, steady day, this brings a jolt of color without asking much of you. The little rover rolling in from the left, ladder and dish on board, has the matter-of-fact air of someone just going about the job.","bright-mid":"The hopefulness you feel runs through the whole design, from the bold yellow MARS to the travel-brochure line \"Multiple Tours Available.\" It imagines a far place as somewhere easy and welcoming to visit.","heavy-charged":"Your tension finds some kinship in the jagged black crack splitting the great pale planet and the sharp zigzags overhead. But the poster channels that charge into play, so it may help turn a stormy mood toward something brighter.","mid-charged":"Restless energy has plenty to do here: arrows streak across the planet, a target-like eye glows at the center, and towers crowd the skyline. It is a picture built to keep an alert mind moving.","bright-charged":"This is your mood in poster form, a burst of red, purple, blue and gold with shapes tumbling over each other. The giant sunny lettering of MARS shouts the same exuberance you feel, with a dash of wonder at the size of it all."}

{"heavy-calm":"This poster will not sit quietly with a somber mood, but its pale blue sky and wide white slope give you a cool, open space to breathe in. Think of it as a window onto clear winter air rather than a mirror of how you feel.","mid-calm":"The two skiers move in matching stride, poles planted at the same angle, and that steady rhythm has an unhurried ease to it. Against the soft blue and white of the hillside, it feels like a long walk with nowhere urgent to be.","bright-calm":"Look at the snow-white hill under a powder blue sky, flat and clean as fresh linen. The skiers are cheerful but never frantic, and the gentle palette lets that warmth settle rather than shout.","heavy-mid":"If your thoughts feel weighty, these two figures offer a simple counterweight: bundled in deep blue, they lean into the climb together. It is less an answer than a reminder that heavy going can be shared.","mid-mid":"There is something reassuringly everyday in the lettering at the bottom, plain capitals stating that they like winter, as if it were the most ordinary fact in the world. The scene matches that tone, two people out doing something good on an ordinary day.","bright-mid":"The red mittens with their white stripes and the hats to match bring a warm, hopeful note to all that cold blue. You can almost feel the easy pleasure of a good day outdoors.","heavy-charged":"The drama in your mood has no storm here to meet it, but the kicked-up puffs of snow at each boot give your restless energy somewhere to go. It is tension turned into forward motion, a way up the hill instead of down.","mid-charged":"Every line pushes forward: the bent knees, the angled poles, the snow spraying from each step. If you are full of energy and alert, this poster moves at your pace.","bright-charged":"Bold blue suits, bright red scarves and a woman's white hair flying behind her in the cold air make this pure exuberance. It shares your joy outright, the thrill of a fresh slope and good company."}

{"heavy-calm":"The pale blue haze where sea meets sky holds almost no edge, and that softness can sit with a quiet, inward mood without asking you to lift out of it. Toorop's fog is gentle rather than gloomy, so it offers stillness first and a little light second.","mid-calm":"Wheel tracks curve slowly across the sandy field, unhurried lines that seem to have been left by someone with nowhere urgent to be. The whole surface moves at that same even pace.","bright-calm":"Built from tiny dots of rose, gold and lavender, the dunes glow with a warm, low light that feels like the end of a mild afternoon. It is a picture at rest, and a kind one.","heavy-mid":"If your thoughts are weighty, the small figure at the right, bent toward the sea with a net raised, may feel familiar: one person working against a vast, blank horizon. Toorop keeps it tender, though, so the gravity never turns harsh.","mid-mid":"A cart on the left, a fisherman on the right, a dog in the grass below: ordinary work and ordinary motion spread across a balanced, level landscape. Nothing is staged, and that steadiness is its charm.","bright-mid":"The fresh green strip of grass along the bottom lifts the whole picture, a hopeful band of color beneath the misty blue. It carries an easy warmth that suits a good mood without overselling it.","heavy-charged":"This painting will not match a storm in you; the sea here is a soft white murmur under fog. What it can offer is a counterweight, a wide, hushed field of dotted color where tension has room to settle.","mid-charged":"The one quick note in the scene is the dog streaking low through the grass, and your restless energy might find it first. Around it, the misty calm of the shore gives that alertness somewhere quieter to land.","bright-charged":"Joy here is quiet rather than loud, but it is present in the shimmer of pink and gold dots across the dunes, like light flickering on sand. Take it as a gentler echo of your lively mood, a place to let the brightness linger."}

{"heavy-calm":"The grey, low sky over the distant water has a hush to it, and the tiger lies beneath it with heavy, half-closed attention. If you are feeling quiet and inward, this is a stillness that keeps its weight without asking anything of you.","mid-calm":"Look at how the long body stretches across the canvas, tail curled loosely at the end, nothing hurried in it. It matches an unhurried mood well: rest that comes easily, at its own pace.","bright-calm":"The warm orange of the fur against the pale belly gives this painting its gentle glow, even under a muted sky. It is not sunny, but it offers the kind of warmth you feel near something large and content, at ease.","heavy-mid":"Andrieu gives the tiger a level, watchful gaze, and that look carries real gravity. For a thoughtful, weighty mood, it holds power held in reserve, something to sit and consider.","mid-mid":"Here is an ordinary moment for an extraordinary animal: lying in the grass, forepaws crossed, simply present. It suits a steady, everyday frame of mind, calm on the surface with quiet alertness underneath.","bright-mid":"The broad, soft brushwork of the grassy slope and the golden coat make this an easy painting to live with. It is more serene than hopeful, but its warmth can meet an easygoing mood halfway.","heavy-charged":"The drama here is all held back, in the dark claws resting against the ground and the cloudy sky rolling in behind. If you feel stormy, this tiger offers tension at rest, a way to hold that charge without letting it break.","mid-charged":"Those large paws, relaxed but ready, hint at how quickly this body could move. For a restless mood, the painting is a counterweight: energy gathered and still, showing you what poise looks like.","bright-charged":"This is not a joyful or lively picture, and it would be honest to say so. What it gives an exuberant mood is the rich amber of the tiger's coat and the awe of a creature this strong choosing to lie still, a calm place to land."}

{"heavy-calm":"If you are feeling low and quiet, the wide, flat blue here asks very little of you, and the small figure under the white umbrella shows how to keep a soft shelter over the things that matter. It is lighter than your mood, but gentle about it.","mid-calm":"The field of even, powdery blue holds everything in place without any fuss, a figure sitting upright on a book with nowhere to rush. It matches an unhurried day well.","bright-calm":"A neat white umbrella, a pale yellow sleeve, and a book drawn in soft wavy lines: this is warmth at rest. Its sweetness is quiet, like yours right now.","heavy-mid":"Arlington Gregg turns a careful thought, that books deserve protection, into a small, upright figure guarding one from the weather. If you are weighing something serious, it offers that same care with a lighter hand.","mid-mid":"The tall, thin capitals of RAIN sit beside a loose white script, plain sense and a bit of charm in balance. It suits an ordinary, steady day.","bright-mid":"The figure's upturned eye and tidy umbrella carry an easy good humor, and the yellow outlines of the book feel almost like sunlight on a gray day. It shares your hopeful, relaxed mood.","heavy-charged":"Where your mood is stormy, this poster keeps the rain outside the frame entirely, leaving only calm blue and a dry, well-kept book. Think of it as a shelter to step into rather than a mirror.","mid-charged":"The wobbly yellow line around the book gives the page edges a little restless shimmer, but the rest of the poster stays composed. It can catch your energy and help it settle.","bright-charged":"The playful pairing of the stern black RAIN with the bouncing handwritten line and its yellow dot has real wit. It is gentler than full exuberance, yet it smiles along with you."}

{"heavy-calm":"The winged figure sits with her cheek on her fist and stares past everything around her, the way stillness feels when it has weight to it. Albrecht Dürer gives your quiet mood a companion who is not trying to get up yet.","mid-calm":"Look at the thin dog curled asleep at her feet, the one creature here fully at rest. It sits a little heavier than an unhurried mood, but that small patch of ease amid the clutter may feel like your own.","bright-calm":"This engraving is darker than your mood, so take it as a counterweight. The rainbow arching over the distant sea is the gentlest thing in it, a soft curve of light you can hold onto while the rest stays shadowed.","heavy-mid":"Here is gravity made into a picture: the hourglass running on the wall, the bell waiting to ring, a compass resting idle in her hand. It matches a thoughtful, weighty mood almost exactly, thinking that has not yet found its answer.","mid-mid":"The grid of numbers on the wall, every row adding up the same, has the steady order of an ordinary day. The brooding figure beside it is heavier than you feel, so the square may be where your eye settles.","bright-mid":"Honestly, this work sits on the somber side of where you are. What it offers a hopeful mood is the comet blazing over the water and the banner lettered MELENCOLIA I, light breaking in from outside the room.","heavy-charged":"Dense crosshatched shadow, an unfinished ladder, and that huge tilted stone block give the scene a held tension rather than a storm. If your drama is the kind that waits and broods, this meets it.","mid-charged":"Restless energy is scattered across the floor here: a saw, nails, a plane, a sphere, tools dropped mid-task. The figure is not moving, but the room around her hums with things left undone, which an alert mind will recognize.","bright-charged":"This is far from joyful, and it does not pretend otherwise. It may serve as a quiet place to land after exuberance, with the small child figure busily scribbling on a slate the one note of lively motion in the room."}

{"heavy-calm":"This is a loud room, and it will not match your stillness. If you want it anyway, look at the grey figure in the foreground: turned away from the dancer and lost in shadow, he is the one quiet, inward presence in the scene.","mid-calm":"The poster runs at a quick pace, but its flat colors are laid down simply and evenly, with broad yellow, black and red. That plainness lets you take in the noise of the dance hall from a restful distance.","bright-calm":"Look at the row of yellow lamps floating over the crowd like small moons. They carry a warm light that sits well with a gentle mood, even while the dancer below kicks up her petticoats.","heavy-mid":"If your thoughts are weighty, the black wall of silhouetted onlookers may hold you first. Their solid dark mass presses in around the bright dancer, a reminder that every celebration has its shadows.","mid-mid":"There is an everyday steadiness under the spectacle: lettering that announces dances every Wednesday and Saturday, like a reliable routine. It suggests that joy can be a weekly habit rather than a rare event.","bright-mid":"The dancer's red polka-dot blouse and her froth of white skirts carry an easy, hopeful cheer. Toulouse-Lautrec makes the evening feel open and welcoming, the kind of night you look forward to.","heavy-charged":"Your stormy energy will find a partner in the stark contrast here, with black crowds, a looming grey figure and red letters shouting across the yellow ground. The tension is real, but it bends toward a dance rather than a fight, and that may give you a way out.","mid-charged":"Moulin Rouge appears three times stacked at the top, as if the poster cannot stop repeating itself. That restless, insistent lettering matches an alert mind that wants to be somewhere, doing something, right now.","bright-charged":"Here is exuberance at full kick: a raised leg, flying white ruffles, and a floor tilting up toward you. Toulouse-Lautrec catches the dance at its highest, most defiant moment, and it shares your joy completely."}

{"heavy-calm":"The frozen canal at the bottom of the scene holds the city's quiet the way you may be holding yours. Nothing moves across that grey ice, and van Troostwijk lets the stillness stand without asking it to lift.","mid-calm":"Look at the hazy church tower fading into the winter air behind the rooftops. It sits at an unhurried distance, a steady point you can rest your eyes on while the rest of the day waits.","bright-calm":"This is a muted winter scene rather than a sunny one, but the soft apricot glow in the clouds above the Raampoortje in Amsterdam gives it warmth. That gentle light may suit a restful mood, even if the cold keeps it a little wistful.","heavy-mid":"A dark arch opens beneath the bridge, and the eye keeps returning to it. Its weight matches a thoughtful, serious frame of mind, set against snow that softens every edge around it.","mid-mid":"Two small figures stand by the wooden railing, going about an ordinary winter morning. Van Troostwijk paints the everyday plainly, with an even hand that suits a balanced day.","bright-mid":"The red roof tiles on the left show through their snow like a small fire kept going. If you are feeling hopeful, this scene offers that hope quietly, as warmth tucked inside a cold city.","heavy-charged":"Nothing here is stormy. The smoke drifts slowly from the chimneys and the ice lies flat, so the painting meets your tension as a counterweight, a place where the pressure has nowhere to go.","mid-charged":"If you are restless, this canal scene will not keep pace with you. The sleigh waiting on the bridge and the still, misty sky offer a pause instead, somewhere for your energy to settle for a moment.","bright-charged":"This is a hushed, slightly melancholy winter morning, far quieter than your high spirits. Still, the snow piled bright along the bridge wall has a crispness that a joyful eye can enjoy, as a cool breath of air."}

{"heavy-calm":"The single dark figure halfway down the hall walks alone between those pale arches, and if you are feeling quiet and inward, his small, steady presence may feel like company rather than sorrow. Van Gogh gives solitude a path to follow.","mid-calm":"Arch after arch repeats in soft lavender and white, each one a little smaller than the last, and that rhythm sets an unhurried pace for the eye. It is a hallway you can walk through slowly.","bright-calm":"This is not a gentle picture at heart; the corridor holds a quiet unease. Still, the warm ochre of the vaulted ceiling glows like late afternoon, and that warmth may be the part that meets your restful mood.","heavy-mid":"Van Gogh painted this corridor while living inside it, and the long red floor pulling toward a far doorway carries real weight. For a thoughtful, grave mood, it offers a place to stand and consider where a long passage leads.","mid-mid":"Look at how plainly the floor is built from strokes of brick red and green, laid down like ordinary tiles on an ordinary day. The scene is everyday architecture, held steady by its even rows of columns.","bright-mid":"At the very end of the hall a small pale doorway opens into light. The mood here leans wistful more than hopeful, but that bright opening is a fair promise for someone feeling easy and forward-looking.","heavy-charged":"The tension in this work lives in its pull: arches crowding inward, the floor tilting slightly, a lone figure moving into the narrowing distance. If your mood is stormy, this shares its tightness without tipping into chaos.","mid-charged":"Nothing in the corridor sits still; the ochre walls are scored with quick, restless brushmarks and the blue edges of the arches seem to flicker. Your alert energy will find plenty to move along with here.","bright-charged":"Honestly, this is a more pensive work than a joyful one. What it can give your lively mood is its color, that sunlit yellow and those flashes of sky blue, which keep even a hospital hallway humming."}

{"heavy-calm":"This poster runs warmer and louder than your mood, but look at the top edge: a dark window full of quiet stars and a blue planet drifting past. It offers a small, still view out of the heaviness, with the cheerful cards waiting below whenever you feel ready.","mid-calm":"Under all the bright cards is a deep black cockpit, and a single gloved hand holding one postcard up to look at it. That unhurried gesture, like sorting old travel souvenirs, suits a restful pace even if the colors run hotter than you do.","bright-calm":"The old-fashioned 'Greetings from' lettering has the gentle warmth of a postcard from someone who misses you. Its cream and red letters keep things friendly and light, though the sunburst above carries more spark than a resting mood needs.","heavy-mid":"If your thoughts feel weighty, the small words 'Since 1995' on the orange card are worth a pause. They mark a real discovery, a first world found around another star, and the poster treats that serious fact with a lightness that might ease your own.","mid-mid":"Here is an ordinary, everyday pleasure: a scatter of postcards on a dashboard, one picked up for a closer look. The steady, balanced layout of cards and lettering makes even a distant planet feel like something you could pin by your desk.","bright-mid":"The orange sunburst behind '51 Pegasi b' radiates outward like good news arriving. It shares your warm, hopeful mood, a promise of somewhere new that feels easy to reach.","heavy-charged":"The storm you feel has no echo here; this poster is pure cheer. Still, the black void framing the cards and the hand reaching from the shadows give your tension a place to land before the bright colors pull you toward something lighter.","mid-charged":"Every card in this pile seems to compete for your eye, a red sticker, a green card with a blazing white star, a figure rocketing off in a jet seat. That busy, layered energy matches a restless mind that wants to go everywhere at once.","bright-charged":"Bold red letters shout 'First Exoplanet' across the bottom like a celebration banner, and the rays of orange above it burst with the same joy. It is a postcard from a whole new world, as lively and exuberant as you feel right now."}

{"heavy-calm":"The pale old figure beside the painter holds up an hourglass, and the sand keeps falling while he sits perfectly still. If you are feeling quiet and inward, this is a portrait that already knows about endings and meets them calmly.","mid-calm":"Look at the painter's faint, settled half-smile as he rests his palette in his lap. Nothing here hurries, and the dim brown room around him moves at the same unhurried pace you are in.","bright-calm":"This one sits further toward shadow than your mood, but the soft lavender of the painter's robe carries a gentle warmth through the gloom. It could offer you a still, reflective counterpoint to a light day without pulling you down.","heavy-mid":"A scythe blade curves across the stone ledge, just below the lines of verse carved there. Van Musscher painted himself beside it on purpose, a grave and thoughtful meditation on how long a painter's work outlasts him.","mid-mid":"Here is a working man at his everyday task, maulstick and palette in hand, framed in a plain arched window. The weighty symbols around him are there, yet his steady gaze keeps the whole picture level and composed.","bright-mid":"Your hopeful mood finds an ally in the small grey cherub at the left, who lifts an arm almost playfully against the heavy curtain. The painting itself leans melancholy, so it offers warmth mostly through that little gesture and the painter's mild, friendly look.","heavy-charged":"The drama here is hushed rather than stormy: a heavy curtain pulled back, and Time leaning in with scythe and hourglass. If you feel tense, this offers a slower kind of gravity, a place to let that charge settle into reflection.","mid-charged":"This is not a restless painting, and it will not match your energy. What it offers instead is the deep, dark recess behind the painter's curls, a still pocket that can steady you when everything feels too quick.","bright-charged":"Honestly, this work runs far quieter and sadder than your joy. Its muted browns and the old man's hourglass could serve as a calm anchor on a wall that sees a lot of liveliness, a reminder to savor the moment you are in."}

{"heavy-calm":"The big oak on the right stands dark and still against the clouds, and its weight matches the quiet inwardness you are carrying. Jules Dupré lets the shadowed road and the pool at its feet sit undisturbed, a place to be somber without being hurried.","mid-calm":"Look past the storm to the small figure in red walking the lit stretch of road. Her unhurried pace is the restful part of this painting, a steady step through weather that has not yet broken.","bright-calm":"This is a heavier sky than your mood, but there is a gentle patch of sunlight falling on the path by the cottage. It offers your lightness a sheltered place to rest while the clouds do the brooding.","heavy-mid":"The low thatched cottage hunkers under a sky thick with greys and ochres, and that sense of a house bracing itself matches the gravity you feel. Dupré paints weather as something to think through, slowly and seriously.","mid-mid":"Everyday life carries on here: a cottage, a road, a woman walking home before the rain. The tension in the clouds is real, but the scene keeps its footing, much as a steady day holds even when the sky shifts.","bright-mid":"Your hopeful mood will find its foothold in the breaks of blue overhead and the warm light spilling onto the road. The storm is present, yet the painting keeps leaving room for that clearing.","heavy-charged":"The clouds churn in heavy, worked paint, and the wind-bent tree at the left edge shows the gust arriving. If your feelings are stormy, this canvas meets them directly, with drama gathered and held just before release.","mid-charged":"There is restless energy in how Dupré builds the sky, thick strokes of cream and slate pushing against each other. Your alertness shares that charge, the feeling of watching weather move in.","bright-charged":"This is not a joyful painting, and it will not echo your exuberance. What it offers is a counterweight: the solemn oak and darkened pond can ground a bright, lively mood, with one shaft of light on the road to keep your spark company."}

{"heavy-calm":"Every candle on this shelf has gone out, and the old lanterns stand in a deep green dark that asks nothing of you. If you are feeling somber and inward, Peto's crowded shelf keeps you company without trying to cheer you up.","mid-calm":"Nothing here moves; the brass candlesticks and tin lamps simply rest where they were left along the plain wooden shelf. That stillness suits an unhurried mood, though the dim light carries a quiet melancholy beneath the calm.","bright-calm":"This is a darker painting than your mood, but the soft gleam on the brass and the pale stubs of candle wax hold a small, warm glow. Think of it as a gentle shadow beside your lightness rather than a match for it.","heavy-mid":"Peto painted a shelf of lamps that no longer light anything, a quiet record of what time leaves behind. For a grave, thoughtful frame of mind, those worn and toppled objects give your reflection something solid to rest on.","mid-mid":"The sturdy shelf and its two simple brackets keep this jumble of old lights in steady order. It leans more wistful than everyday, yet that plain, carpentered structure gives it a grounded, even feel.","bright-mid":"Your hopeful mood will find this painting more wistful than warm. Still, the honeyed brass of the candlesticks catches what light there is, a reminder that fondness for the past can sit alongside an easy present.","heavy-charged":"There is no storm here, only a lantern dangling off the shelf's edge and a candlestick knocked on its side. Those small tumbles hint at disorder, but the hushed dark around them offers a slower place to set down your tension.","mid-charged":"If you feel restless, this is a counterweight more than a mirror: dozens of lamps and candleholders crowd together, yet all of them are cold and silent. Your eye can roam the clutter while the stillness slows you down.","bright-charged":"Your joy runs well ahead of this painting, which is hushed, dim, and fond of things gone by. What it can offer is contrast, the unlit candles and murky green ground setting off your own bright energy like a quiet room at the end of a lively day."}

{"heavy-calm":"The deep navy shadows pooled in the canyon's lower folds hold a stillness close to yours, even as pink light rests on the rim above. You can stay in the dark parts of this view and still see the day going on overhead.","mid-calm":"Layer after layer of flat-topped rock steps down in an even rhythm, like slow breathing. Nothing here hurries, and the eye moves across it at its own pace.","bright-calm":"Soft pink clouds drift over a rose-washed rim, a gentle, warm light that seems to settle rather than shine. It keeps you company in an easy, restful mood.","heavy-mid":"The great central butte stands with real weight, its shadowed purple flanks carved deep by time. It offers you a scale for serious thoughts, something old and patient to think beside.","mid-mid":"Plain block lettering, a small buffalo emblem, and a view laid out clearly from rim to river: this is a steady, unfussy poster. It sits well in an ordinary day, quietly reminding you the canyon is there.","bright-mid":"\"A Free Government Service\" reads the top line, an open invitation printed in the same warm pink as the cliffs.
